title: Redwood Controls quality-of-earnings normalization
prompt:
Prepare Redwood Controls' LTM quality-of-earnings bridge for investment committee and recommend the earnings basis for valuation.

Use the July corporate-development investment-committee correspondence, the 7/5 controller-tied IC book, the current data-room export, the diligence review notes, and the approved underwriting policy. Treat the 6/29 banker case as change history only.

Rebuild LTM revenue and reported EBITDA from Redwood's twelve-month target P&L. Compare July through December with January through June, and use the latest quarter and annualized run rates to assess whether the normalized earnings basis is supported by recent performance. Keep these run-rate diagnostics separate from QoE adjustments.

Treat the seller's headline adjustments as proposals. Independently size each item from the compensation, settlement, vacancy, procurement, and facility evidence, classify the proposals, and bridge each difference between the seller and underwriting cases. Reconcile seller-adjusted EBITDA to supported normalized EBITDA without a plug.

Keep residual risk separate from normalized QoE. Rank the risks by probability-weighted EBITDA impact, build seller-adjusted, normalized, and risk-adjusted valuation cases at the working entry multiple, and show both valuation haircuts. State which earnings case should anchor valuation and how the risk-adjusted case should be used.

Do not modify files or post transactions. Return only one JSON object with exactly these keys: `ltm_revenue`, `reported_ebitda`, `jul_dec_revenue`, `jan_jun_revenue`, `jul_dec_reported_ebitda`, `jan_jun_reported_ebitda`, `jul_dec_reported_ebitda_margin`, `jan_jun_reported_ebitda_margin`, `jan_jun_revenue_growth_vs_jul_dec`, `jan_jun_ebitda_growth_vs_jul_dec`, `jan_jun_annualized_reported_ebitda`, `jan_jun_annualized_headroom_to_normalized_ebitda`, `latest_quarter_revenue`, `latest_quarter_reported_ebitda`, `latest_quarter_reported_ebitda_margin`, `latest_quarter_annualized_reported_ebitda`, `latest_quarter_annualized_headroom_to_normalized_ebitda`, `seller_proposed_adjustments`, `seller_adjusted_ebitda`, `seller_adjusted_ebitda_margin`, `owner_compensation_adjustment`, `legal_settlement_adjustment`, `vacant_cfo_adjustment`, `accepted_adjustments`, `rejected_adjustments`, `net_accepted_adjustments`, `owner_compensation_seller_to_underwriting_gap`, `legal_settlement_seller_to_underwriting_gap`, `vacant_cfo_seller_to_underwriting_gap`, `procurement_synergy_seller_to_underwriting_gap`, `facility_savings_seller_to_underwriting_gap`, `normalized_ebitda`, `normalized_ebitda_margin`, `seller_to_underwriting_ebitda_gap`, `working_entry_multiple`, `seller_to_underwriting_enterprise_value_gap`, `largest_remaining_qoe_risk`, `largest_risk_expected_impact`, `technician_attrition_expected_impact`, `deferred_maintenance_expected_impact`, `remaining_risk_ranking`, `aggregate_probability_weighted_risk`, `largest_risk_share_of_aggregate`, `risk_adjusted_ebitda`, `risk_adjusted_ebitda_margin`, `seller_adjusted_enterprise_value`, `normalized_enterprise_value`, `risk_adjusted_enterprise_value`, `risk_overlay_enterprise_value_haircut`, `seller_to_risk_adjusted_enterprise_value_gap`, `risk_adjusted_enterprise_value_pct_of_normalized`, `recommended_valuation_earnings_basis`, `recommended_residual_risk_treatment`. Use dollars to two decimals, ratios and percentages as decimal ratios to at least four decimals, and lists as JSON arrays.
